record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth algebraic variety diffeomorphic to C^n. If X is biholomorphic to C^n, must X already be isomorphic to C^n?

evidence.quote:
2.5. CONJECTURE. Let X be a smooth algebraic variety diffeomorphic to Cn. If
X is biholomorphic to Cn, then it is isomorphic to Cn.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be a smooth complex algebraic variety of dimension $n$ that is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$ (regarded as a real $2n$-dimensional smooth manifold). Suppose further that $X$, viewed as a complex analytic manifold, is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$. Must $X$ then be isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$ as an algebraic variety?
artifact.category_tag: Affine algebraic geometry / characterizations of affine space
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a well-known conjecture in affine algebraic geometry concerning exotic algebraic structures on complex affine space. No general resolution appears in the literature; constructions of exotic algebraic structures on $\mathbb{C}^n$ (e.g. by Ramanujam, tom Dieck–Petrie, Zaidenberg) exist but are not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$, and the characterization of the affine space among smooth varieties biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$ remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (problems list)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: a smooth algebraic variety diffeomorphic to C^n and biholomorphic to C^n is isomorphic to C^n.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as a conjecture in a problems collection; no resolution cited.
